info.title: Metalcraft Agent API
info.description: The pod's workshop admin API. Manages personas, skills, flows, keys, chats, diagnostics sessions, integrations, and gateway channels. Authenticate with a Bearer token: the static WORKSHOP_API_KEY or a Metalcraft ID token (mck_…) scoped to this pod.

200.description: The .agentpack bytes, or a report if `out` was given

502.description: The registry could not be reached

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Local .agentpack path; omit to upload the archive as the body

200.description: Origins this pod will download an agent pack from

parameters.name: token_key
parameters.description: Key-store entry to draw the bearer from; defaults to METALCRAFT_TOKEN

Registries come from AGENT_PACK_REGISTRIES and cannot be edited

parameters.description: The pack's handle on that host

400.description: That is not a usable pack id

502.description: The host would not serve it

parameters.name: force
parameters.description: Orphan any saved agents that use it

post.description:
Separate from install because the *consequences* are different: install adds an
agent, update changes agents that already exist and that somebody may be talking
to right now. The report says what followed — and, crucially, names any agent
whose persona or preset the new version withdrew, so the two silent failure modes
become two lines in a dialog.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The installed agent pack to update

200.description: The preset, with its roster resolved

get.summary: Every conversation this agent has had, newest activity first.
get.description:
The same list `GET …/instances/{id}` embeds, on its own route — a session list
reloads whenever a conversation changes, and it has no use for the agent's
memory or its schedules, which that endpoint also pays to assemble.

get.summary: `GET /api/v1/agents/instances/{id}/flows` — what this agent is scheduled to do.
get.description:
The same list `GET …/instances/{id}` embeds, on its own route. It is worth its own
endpoint because it is the question somebody asks right before they decide whether
to trust a background agent, and answering it should not mean fetching an agent's
whole conversation index.

200.description: Flow schedules armed to this agent
What this agent knows, shipped vs learned

get.summary:
List all channels — the built-in `metalcraft` default first, then custom
channels. Secrets are never included.

post.summary:
Add a custom channel (its own gateway url + secret). The `metalcraft` slug is
reserved for the built-in channel.

put.summary: Update a custom channel. The built-in `metalcraft` channel can't be edited.

delete.summary:
Delete a custom channel and its secret. The built-in `metalcraft` channel
can't be deleted.

get.summary: Recent activity for a single channel (by slug), newest first.

post.description:
Deliberately does everything an automatic compaction does, including handing
the summary to memory: it is the most concentrated account of the conversation
that will ever exist and the LLM call is already paid for, so a forced
compaction that dropped it would quietly be worth less than one that happened
by itself.

Refuses mid-turn. Compaction rewrites the message list the running turn is
reading, and "your context changed under you" is not a failure mode worth
having.

get.summary:
What this chat's context costs right now — the read behind `/tokens`, and the
number a client needs to show headroom before someone hits the wall.

Live subscription to a chat's *agent-initiated* turns (scheduled follow-ups).
The workshop opens this when a chat is on screen so a follow-up that fires
while the user is idle streams in without a page refresh. Normal
user-initiated turns still come back on their own `POST .../turn` response.

200.description: SSE stream of agent-initiated ChatEvent frames

post.summary: Ask a running turn to stop — the client's stop button.
post.description:
Returns as soon as the request is recorded, not when the turn ends: the
executor notices at its next step boundary and finishes the turn itself,
emitting `done{status:"interrupted"}` on the chat's event stream. That frame,
not this response, is what says the agent has actually stopped.

Interrupting is resumable by construction — the guard stops the executor
between steps, so the partial state is written back like any other turn and
the next message continues from it. Nothing is discarded.

post.summary: End this conversation's context without ending the conversation — `/reset`.
post.description:
The agent starts its next turn from nothing, and the transcript gains a
divider where that happened. Nothing is deleted: this used to be `/clear`,
which dropped the history outright because the transcript and the context were
the same list and there was nowhere else for it to live. `DELETE /chats/{id}`
is still how a conversation actually goes away.

Refuses mid-turn, like compaction: pulling the context out from under a
running turn is not a failure mode worth having.

post.summary:
Run one turn against the chat session. Streams new messages as Server-Sent
Events as the agent steps; closes the connection when the executor returns.

202.description: A turn was already running: the message is queued and will run next. Its frames arrive on `GET /chats/{id}/events`, not on this response.

get.summary: The OTLP trace for one session — where a turn's time actually went.
get.description:
Deliberately separate from `GET /diagnostics/{id}`: that response already
carries every message of every turn, and a trace is read for timings, often
while the session's transcript is already on screen. Bundling them would make
the common read pay for the large one.

`404` covers both "no such session" and "that session has no trace" — a run
from before tracing existed reads the same way to a client, which has nothing
to show either way.

post.summary: Erase this pod and restart it as if it had just been provisioned.
post.description:
Answers **before** it exits, and the report it returns is the last word this
process says — anything the client wants to know about what was removed has
to come from here, because the next thing to answer on this port will be a
pod with no history of the request.

500.description: Could not read the data directory; nothing was removed

get.summary: List persisted flow runs, optionally filtered by `?flow_id=`.
Get one flow run by id.
`GET /api/v1/flows` — every flow on this pod.
get.description:
The listing the API never had: until now a client had to already know a flow's
id to see anything at all, which made "show me what this pod is set up to do"
unanswerable. See `docs/FLOWS_AS_AGENTS_PLAN.md` §3.

200.description: Every flow installed on this pod

post.summary:
Install a registry flow onto this agent: download its `SavedFlow` JSON from
flows.metalcraftai.com, validate it, and save it into the flows dir (installed
disabled). Returns `{ flow, dependencies }` — the dependency report lists any
packs/personas the flow needs that aren't installed yet.
Check a flow graph without persisting it.
post.description:
`PUT /flows/{id}` already validates before saving and is still the authority —
this exists so an editor can say what is wrong *while someone is typing*,
which is the only time the answer can still change what they do. Same
`metalcraft_flows::validate` behind both, so the two can never disagree.

Not a 400: an invalid graph is the expected answer to this question, not a bad
request. The status says the check ran; the body says what it found.

400.description: The graph is invalid; the body lists why

409.description: The flow changed since it was loaded — `updated_at` does not match

400.description: Flow names personas outside the roster

post.summary:
Report whether this pod satisfies the integrations an already-installed flow
declares in its `requires` block. One outcome per pack.
post.description:
It reports rather than installs. Fetching a pack from here was a second install
path into a second layout; an integration reaches a pod inside an agent pack the
operator installs, through `POST /api/v1/agent-packs/install` and nowhere else.

200.description: v2 flows return a FlowRunSummary; v1 flows return a RunFlowResponse

get.summary:
Recent gateway activity across all channels, including inbound messages that
matched no channel (the global Network view). Newest first.

post.summary: Connect: fetch config + wire the webhook + enable the channel. 409 until verified.
Disconnect: disable the metalcraft-gateway channel + drop its secrets. Idempotent.
Inline register: proxy to the gateway with the pod's token; returns `verify_code`.

get.summary: Registration/verification/connection state for the workshop's Connect panel.

post.summary: Unregister: give the number back at the gateway, then disconnect locally.
post.description:
The exit that `disconnect` is not. Disconnecting stops this pod receiving and
leaves the account's registration standing — number still bound and verified,
dedicated number still out of the pool, managed integration still routing to
a consumer that left. This is the one that ends all of that, and until it
existed only a client holding the account PAT could do it, which excludes
every client that reaches the account through its pod.

get.summary:
Agent identity/version + config the Workshop reads. `version` drives the
Settings tab's "which build is live" check; `default_persona` is the persona
the Workshop's New Chat modal defaults to (set `METALCRAFT_DEFAULT_PERSONA`
to override; falls back to the orchestrator, which delegates to specialists).

200.description: Agent name, version, and default persona

put.summary:
Retired. An integration is no longer independently enabled or disabled —
an agent pack is the install unit, and the packs it vendors are simply present
(see `docs/AGENT_PACKS_PLAN.md`).
put.description:
This answers 410 rather than quietly succeeding: a toggle that returns 204 and
changes nothing is worse than one that says it is gone, because the UI would go
on showing a state the runtime does not honour.

410.description: Retired — uninstall the agent pack instead

get.summary:
Keys recommended by enabled packs, each flagged configured/missing. Lets the
key store UI surface "these enabled packs need these keys" without the user
having to read each pack's manifest.

put.summary:
Upsert a key. The name comes from the path; the raw value (and an optional
target `channel_id`) from the body. Managed keys — a platform-injected global
(env-authoritative) or a provisioner-backed channel's secrets — are read-only
and rejected here.

delete.summary:
Delete a key. An optional `?channel_id=` targets a channel's secret scope;
omitted means the global scope. Managed keys are read-only and rejected.

parameters.name: channel_id
parameters.description: Channel scope for a channel secret

get.summary:
Reveal a stored key's **raw** value. An optional `?channel_id=` targets a
channel's secret scope; omitted means global. This is the one endpoint that
returns an unmasked value — an explicit, user-initiated action in the Keys UI.
Only returns values physically present in the store (a derived/env-only value
like a provisioner's `API_KEY` is not stored, so there's nothing to reveal).

parameters.name: channel_id
parameters.description: Channel scope for a channel secret

get.summary:
The pod's `metalcraft.lock` — every registry pack/flow pinned to an exact
version + content hash. Export it to clone a pod's toolset, or feed it to
`/lockfile/restore` on a rebuilt pod.

post.summary:
Reinstall everything in the lockfile at its pinned version, verifying each against
its locked content hash — the reproducible-rebuild path for a fresh or cloned pod.
Returns one outcome per entry; a failure on one entry doesn't stop the rest.

get.summary: Every persona on this pod: the pod's own, plus those an enabled pack vendors.
get.description:
Locals shadow packs on a slug collision, which is the same precedence the
runner resolves with — so what is listed here is what would actually run.

Summaries only. A persona's system prompt is most of its bytes and none of an
index's job; `GET /personas/{slug}` is the whole document.

get.summary: `GET /api/v1/scheduled-flows` — everything this pod will do on its own.
get.description:
The complete answer: nothing else fires a flow on a timer. An empty list means
this pod does nothing unless somebody asks it to.

parameters.name: instance_id
parameters.description: Only schedules armed to this agent.

post.description:
This is the consent point: it creates the schedule **and** the agent that will
run it, since "run this while nobody is watching" is one decision rather than
two. Schedules of one flow share an agent unless `instance_id` says
otherwise, so the evening run remembers the morning one.

400.description: Bad trigger, or a persona outside the flow's roster

post.description:
Takes an unsaved spec so an editor can answer the question before committing to
it. An empty `next_runs` on a cron trigger means this pod cannot parse it — the
thing a person most needs to know before saving.

delete.description:
**The agent and everything it remembers are kept.** Disarming is "stop running
this on a timer", not "destroy the thing that was running it", and a client
should not imply otherwise.

204.description: Disarmed; the agent and its memory are kept

get.summary: List scheduled follow-ups (pending + recently completed), newest first.
What this pod is to Octaweave, and whether the tools are installed.
get.description:
A read, not a write: there is nothing to configure. The pod presents the Metalcraft
token it already holds, and the only human step is linking the two accounts once —
which happens on Octaweave's own page, at `link_url`.

get.summary: What this pod is set to prefer.

put.summary: Replace them. The whole document, so clearing a preference is expressible.

400.description: A preference this pod cannot honour, e.g. an unknown timezone

get.summary: Every skill on this pod: the pod's own, plus those an enabled pack vendors.
get.description:
Summaries only — a skill *is* its markdown body, so an index that carried it
would be the whole skills directory in one response. `GET /skills/{slug}` has
the body.

get.summary:
Every timezone this pod can resolve, grouped by region — the list a picker
should offer.
get.description:
Published rather than left to each client's own platform list, because the
two drift: a zone the phone knows and this build of the tz database does not
is a save that fails *after* somebody chose it.

agent_pack.description: The agent pack that provided the preset, when it came from one.

agent_preset.description:
The agent preset this instance was created from. **Immutable for its life** —
its memory is seeded from that preset, so swapping it mid-life is incoherent.
Switching agents means starting a new instance.

created_from_version.description:
Diagnostics only. Personas and skills **follow** the installed pack version
(see the plan's §5.4); this records what it was born against.

orphaned_from.description:
Set when the agent pack that provided this agent's preset withdrew it — on
update or on a forced uninstall. The agent keeps its memory and its
conversations and goes on working against a frozen copy of the preset; this
records what happened, so a UI can say so rather than presenting a
pack-provided agent that is quietly no longer pack-provided.

persona.description:
The instance's current persona — starts at the preset's default and moves
within its roster.

persona_fallback_from.description:
Set when an update withdrew the persona this agent was using and it fell back
to the preset's default. Reported rather than silent: the agent's voice
changed, and nobody asked for that.

content_sha256.description:
Hash of every file in the archive **except `agent_pack.json`**, so the
manifest can carry the hash of what it describes without hashing itself.

handle.description: The registry handle this pack is published under (`amy_kitchen`).

oneOf.description: Fork lineage.

presets.description:
The agent presets this pack provides. Exactly one today — the registry
enforces it — but an array so multi-preset "crews" stay additive later.

requires_env.description:
Derived at build time and **re-derived at install**; a manifest that
disagrees with its own contents is rejected rather than trusted.

AgentPackPreview.description:
What installing this pack would grant, and what it would change.

The install dialog's whole reason to exist. Without this a client could only
show a permission summary *after* installing, which is not consent — or parse the
archive itself, duplicating the validator that has to be authoritative anyway.

Everything here is derived from the archive's own bytes. The consent summary
never comes from what the author wrote about their pack.

content_sha256.description:
Content hash of the archive as received, so a UI can show what it is about to
install and compare it against what a registry advertised.

installed_version.description:
The version already installed under this id, if any. Present means this is an
upgrade (or a downgrade), not a first install, and the dialog should say so.

missing_env.description:
Credentials the pod does not have yet. A warning, not a blocker: the pack
installs and its tools fail clearly at call time until `key_set` fixes it.

preset.description: The single preset this pack provides.

preset_collisions.description: Preset slugs another installed pack already provides.

source.description: Where the bytes came from — a URL, a path, or `"upload"`.

delegates_to_any_persona.description:
**Unrestricted delegation.** Normally a preset's `sub_agent` calls are
confined to [`Self::callable_personas`] — the roster it declared. An
orchestrator-style preset is the exception: its whole job is to hand work to
whichever specialist fits, including personas that arrived later with an agent
pack it has never heard of. With this set, every persona installed on the pod
joins its delegation roster (its own still listed first).

It is a real widening of what the agent can reach, so it stays opt-in per
preset and is logged when an agent pack ships a preset that claims it.

integrations.description:
Reads `integration_packs` too — the pre-0.30 name, still present in every
preset authored before the rename.

library.description:
**A library, not an agent.** The preset exists to carry a persona roster,
skills and integrations into the pod; nothing about it is startable. No
instance may be minted from it, it is not offered in a picker, and no flow
may be bound to it.

This is what an agent pack sets when its value is the specialist it ships
rather than a dedicated agent to talk to. Nothing is lost by it: the
personas and skills install exactly as before, and `general-agent`
([`Self::delegates_to_any_persona`]) reaches every persona on the pod — so
the orchestrator can still hand work to the specialist. What goes away is
the "start a new agent as this" entry that nobody wanted to pick.

Enforced at the doors that mint an [`AgentInstance`] rather than in
[`Self::load`], because resolving a persona or skill through this preset is
precisely what must keep working.

[`AgentInstance`]: crate::agent_instance::AgentInstance

ArmConsent.description: The resolved content of the arm dialog.

base_memories.description: Seed memories the agent starts from. It accumulates more on every run.

missing_env.description:
Credentials the pod does not have — those tools will fail at 3am rather than
at a moment anyone is looking.

mutating_tools.description: Tools that can change something on the other end.

preset_name.description: Display name of the preset this flow runs as.

instance_name.description: Absent if the instance was deleted out from under it.

name.description:
Its label, so the arm dialog can say *which* schedule without showing an
opaque id.

sub.description: The author's Metalcraft ID subject, when the registry recorded one.

preset.description: The preset slug. `null` clears the binding back to the default agent.

Channel.description:
A channel as surfaced to callers/UI: a named connection. `managed` marks the
built-in `metalcraft` channel (secret is the pod token; not user-editable).
The secret value itself is never included here.

active_number.description: The gateway number bound to this channel, if any.

agent_preset.description:
The agent that answers inbound on this channel. Its instance — and everything
that instance remembers — is what gives the channel continuity across idle
resets. Absent means the pod default.

Without this a channel could only ever be the default agent: installing an
agent pack and pointing an SMS number at it was not expressible, and the
channel's memory base was one that had never been built.

connected.description: Whether the channel has completed a gateway connect (link fields present).

integration_id.description:
The gateway integration UUID this channel is bound to. Inbound messages
carrying this `source_id` route here; also the send-time sender selector.

managed.description: True only for the built-in `metalcraft` channel.

model.description: Model override for inbound runs on this channel.

persona.description: Persona that answers inbound on this channel (default: the agent's own).

ChatCompacted.description: The result of a forced compaction.

compacted.description:
False when there was nothing old enough to summarize — not an error, and
the honest answer for a short conversation.

summary.description: The summary that replaced the old half, when one was produced.

ChatContext.description: What a chat's context currently costs.

compact_threshold_tokens.description: Automatic compaction fires above this. A client can render the headroom.

estimated_tokens.description:
Rough estimate (~4 chars per token), the same one compaction decides on.
Not the provider's count — good enough to answer "how full is this?".

would_compact.description: Whether the next turn would compact on its own.

plan.description:
The plan of the turn running right now, empty when none is. Lets a client
that arrives mid-turn render the plan it missed the frames for.

oneOf.description:
Marks the start of a turn — emitted once at the top of `post_chat_turn`
so the workshop can open a new group in the transcript.

session_id.description:
Diagnostics session directory name for this chat, so the workshop can
deep-link a turn (or a turn error) to its session logs. `None` for a
chat with no active logger — e.g. one reloaded after an agent restart.

oneOf.description: LLM call has started. Paired with a later `LlmCompleted`.

LLM call finished. `messages` is any new assistant message(s); tool
calls produced by this LLM step are emitted as separate `ToolStarted`
events immediately after.
A tool the LLM requested is about to run.

The tool finished. `result` is the `ToolResult` message that was
appended to state.

The agent's user-facing message, produced by a `say_to_user` or
`ask_user` tool call. In tool-only mode this — not free-text
`LlmCompleted` content — is the assistant's message; the workshop renders
it as the reply bubble. The underlying tool start/finish events are
suppressed so the reply isn't also shown as a raw tool card.

`awaiting_reply` distinguishes the two ways a turn ends: an answer closes
the exchange, a question leaves it open and the client should invite a
response (and may render `options` as tappable choices). Both are omitted
when unset, so a client written before `ask_user` existed still sees a
perfectly ordinary reply — which is the correct degradation, since the
question is in the text either way.

What the turn is doing *before* the model is called — work that emits no
other frame and that a client would otherwise render as an
undifferentiated wait.

Compaction is a whole extra summarization LLM call and recall is an
embeddings call; both run ahead of the executor, so nothing between
`turn_started` and the first `llm_started` used to say a word. `phase` is
an open string (`crate::runtime::phase`) precisely so a client older than
a phase can drop the frame instead of breaking on it.

A message was accepted while a turn was already running, and is waiting
its turn rather than starting one.

Emitted on the chat's live bus rather than on the sending request, which
has already been answered with 202 — the point of queueing is that the
sender does not hold a connection open waiting. `position` is 1 for the
next message to run.

This turn's plan, as `update_plan` wrote it. Sent on every change,
including the empty list a new turn starts with, so a client renders the
plan as it stands rather than accumulating every version of it.

A queued message joined the turn that was already running, rather than
waiting for it to end. The client should stop showing it as pending.
Terminal event. `status` is "completed" | "interrupted" | "failed".

A classified turn failure, safe to show the user. Emitted instead of a
bare `Done{status:"failed"}` so frontends can render a friendly message
(and branch on `code`) rather than the raw provider-error chain. `code`
is the machine-readable identifier (see `runtime::ErrorCode`); `message`
is the user-facing text; `retryable` hints whether "try again" is useful.
A `done` still follows so lifecycle handling is unchanged for old clients.

The conversation's context ended — see [`ChatMessageWire::Reset`].

Not part of a turn's lifecycle: it arrives on its own, usually with nobody
having typed anything. Without it a client watching a flow's agent would
see the 3am firing start from nothing and have no way to say why, since
the divider it should draw is only in the transcript it loaded hours ago.

ChatEvent.description:
SSE event wire format. One JSON object per event. The `kind` field
discriminates; payloads vary by kind. Events form a lifecycle:
  `turn_started` → `phase`* → (`llm_started` → `llm_completed`
                  → `tool_started`* → `tool_completed`*)+
                  → `done`
(`tool_started` and `tool_completed` can repeat per LLM step; `phase` frames
cover the pre-model work that would otherwise be silent.)

stopping.description:
True when a turn was running and has been asked to stop. False when the
chat was already idle — the turn finished on its own between the press
and this request, which is not a failure and must not be shown as one.

oneOf.description:
A reasoning item preserved so it can be replayed with its tool call on a
later turn (Responses API requirement for reasoning models). Persisted so
the pairing survives a reload — dropping it would re-trigger the "function
call without required reasoning item" 400 on resume.

A conversation boundary: everything above it is history the model no
longer sees.

The only wire message with no `AgentMessage` counterpart, and that is the
whole point of it. A reset ends a *context*, not a session — the transcript
keeps everything and the context restarts here.

Distinct from the other way a context gets cleared, which is a *new
session* under the same agent (what a gateway conversation does after a
quiet gap). That one leaves no divider because there is nothing to divide:
it is a different conversation. This is for a clean slate inside the
conversation you are already in. `reason` is short free text shown on the
divider, so a transcript can answer "why does my history stop here".

ChatMessageWire.description:
Wire form for `metalcraft::AgentMessage` — the in-memory enum isn't
`Serialize`, so we convert before responding. Also used as the on-disk
format for persisted chats, so it derives `Deserialize` too.

ChatQueued.description: The answer to a turn request that arrived mid-turn: taken, not started.

position.description: Place in line, 1 for the next message to run.

queued.description:
Always true. Present so a client can branch on the body rather than on
the status code, which is easy to lose through a wrapper.

instance_id.description:
The agent this conversation belongs to. `None` only on records written before
instances existed, until the startup backfill reaches them.

Exposed because a client cannot group conversations by agent without it —
which is the whole shape of the chat list once agents exist, and the summary
was the one place it was missing.

preview.description:
The start of the *last* thing said, trimmed to one line — what makes a
row identifiable as *this* conversation rather than a timestamp beside an
id, and what tells you where it got to.

turn_count.description:
How many times the user spoke. The unit a person counts a conversation in
— not messages, which counts the agent's tool chatter, and not the
transcript length, which now also counts reset dividers.

updated_at.description:
Last activity, from the chat file's mtime — [`persist_chat`] rewrites it
after every turn, so it is the clock the pod already trusts for staleness
(see [`gateway_session_is_stale`]). `None` when the file cannot be read.

A list sorted by `created_at` puts a conversation someone has been in all
day below one they opened this morning and abandoned, which is the wrong
way round for the question a session list answers.

Connection.description: What this pod is to one registry.

account.description: Whatever the host will say about the account — an email, usually.

detail.description:
The host's own words when something went wrong, for a UI to show verbatim
instead of inventing an explanation.

link_url.description:
Where a human goes to finish the connection. Taken from the host's own answer
rather than assembled here: a URL we guessed is a URL we would still be sending
people to after the host moved it.

token_key.description:
The key-store entry this registry draws its bearer from — the name, never the
value.

ConnectionState.description: How far a registry connection got, in the only terms a UI can act on.

ConsentSummary.description: What a human is shown before approving an install.

domains.description: Every origin this agent's tools can reach.

mutating_tools.description:
Tools classified as mutating. A read-only agent is a materially smaller
commitment than one that can write, and the dialog should say which it is.

requires_env.description: Every credential it wants, and what wants it.

tools.description: Tool names it gains, so "what can this thing actually do" is answerable.

agent_preset.description: The agent to start this conversation with. Defaults to `general-agent`.

instance_id.description:
Continue an existing agent instead of minting a new one — how a named agent
accumulates conversations.

name.description:
Name the agent. A label only — nothing about an agent's lifetime follows
from it, and nothing deletes an agent on a timer.

persona_slug.description:
Optional now: with an `agent_preset`, the persona comes from the preset's
default. Kept for callers that still pick a persona directly.

enabled.description:
Start firing immediately. Defaults to `true` — creating a schedule is the
act of asking for it; a client staging one passes `false`.

from_suggestion.description:
The author's suggestion key, when the person accepted a suggested schedule
from a pack or the registry.

id.description:
A hand-chosen id instead of a generated one. Rejected on collision: a create
must never overwrite an existing schedule.

instance_id.description:
Attach to an existing agent instead of minting one — e.g. run the briefer as
the same agent you chat with.

DependencyReport.description: What a flow needs beyond itself, checked against this agent's current state.

missing_packs.description: Of `required_packs`, those not installed *and enabled* on this agent.

missing_personas.description: Of `required_personas`, those not available on this agent.

required_env.description: Secret keys the required (installed) packs declare in their `requires_env`.

required_packs.description:
Integrations the flow requires — the union of what the graph
references (`sub_agent.pack` + custom vendor nodes) and what the flow's
`requires` block declares.

required_personas.description: Personas the flow's nodes run as (`data.persona`).

required_tools.description: Tool names the flow's `tool` nodes invoke (the real API surface).

version_conflicts.description:
Version/hash conflicts: a required pack is installed & enabled but its
version is outside the declared range, or its content hash doesn't match a
pin. Human-readable, one per conflict (advisory — install never hard-fails).

DiagnosticsSession.description:
A fully reconstructed session: its `session_info.json` plus an ordered
timeline of every other JSON event file in the directory.

DiagnosticsSessionSummary.description: One session in the listing (metadata + turn count, no per-turn payloads).

flow_id.description: Present (and `kind == "flow"`) when produced by a flow run.

instance_id.description:
The agent this session belongs to. Absent on sessions written before agents
existed, and on CLI runs, which have no agent.

This is what lets a Sessions list answer "which agent produced this?" — the
question that matters most for a background agent, whose failures arrive here
with nobody watching.

kind.description: "session" for a normal run, "flow" for a flow run.

turn_count.description: Count of `turn_NNN.json` files — how far the run actually got.

EnvRequirement.description:
One credential, attributed to what needs it — because the question a human is
answering at install time is "which secrets do I have to paste in", not "which
pack wants what".

out.description: Write the archive here. Omit to receive the bytes in the response.

confirm.description:
Must be exactly `FACTORY RESET`. A typed phrase rather than a flag, so
that nothing reaches this endpoint by accident — see
[`crate::factory_reset::CONFIRM_PHRASE`].

scope.description:
Defaults to [`ResetScope::Full`], the scope that actually reproduces a
new pod. `keep_keys` is the convenience option and the weaker test.

FlowBindingView.description: The binding for one flow, resolved for display.

armed.description: The schedules of this flow that are armed to an agent.

bound.description: True when the preset was chosen deliberately rather than defaulted.

consent.description:
Everything the arm dialog needs to state what arming this actually permits.

Arming is the second consent moment, and the sharper one: a scheduled flow
acts **while nobody is watching**, so a mutating tool inside one is a bigger
commitment than the same tool in a chat where an approval prompt exists.

personas.description: Personas the flow names, and whether the preset can reach each one.

preset.description:
The preset the flow runs as. Always populated — an unbound flow resolves to
the default agent, which is what it effectively already was.

FlowDefinition.description: A graph: nodes and the directed edges between them.

edges.description: All directed arcs in the graph.

FlowEdge.description: A directed arc connecting two nodes in a [`FlowDefinition`].

source_handle.description:
Optional named output port on the source node (multi-output nodes
like [`CoreNodeType::Branch`]).

target_handle.description: Optional named input port on the target node.

FlowListItem.description:
One flow, resolved for display.

A flow is *what work is this*: the graph, the agent preset it runs as, and how
many schedules point at it. **When** it runs is not here — that is
`GET /api/v1/scheduled-flows`, one call for the whole pod, which a client joins
against this listing by `flow_id`.

enabled_count.description: Of `scheduled_count`, how many are enabled. Zero means nothing fires.

preset.description:
The preset this flow runs as. Always populated — an unbound flow resolves to
the default agent, which is what it effectively already was.

scheduled_count.description:
How many schedules point at this flow, of which how many are enabled.

Enough for a listing to say "runs twice a day" or "never runs" without
fetching every schedule; a client that wants the triggers themselves reads
`/scheduled-flows`.

v2.description:
v2 flows run on the state-machine executor and `POST /run` answers with a
`FlowRunSummary`; v1 flows answer with the legacy per-prompt response. Worth
knowing before offering a button that has to render one of them.

data.description: Free-form per-node configuration. Schema depends on `node_type`.

position.description: `[x, y]` coordinates for visual editors. Defaults to `[0.0, 0.0]`.

FlowNodeType.description: A core node type (entry, prompt, conditional, branch, set_variable, tool, http, sub_agent, approval, wait, foreach, end, branch_tool) or a vendor-namespaced custom type such as `slack:send_message`. Custom types are opaque and must round-trip unchanged.

FlowPromptResult.description: Result of running one prompt node of a flow.

chat_id.description:
The conversation this run is writing itself into, so a resumed run
continues the thread it paused in rather than starting a stranger's.
Absent when the run has no agent (nothing to record into) or never reached
a node that spoke.

current_node_id.description: The node the run is paused at (for `paused`) or last ran.

oneOf.description:
Snapshot of the flow definition at pause time, so resume routes against
the graph the run actually paused in — not a since-edited on-disk flow.
Absent (`None`) on legacy records; resume then falls back to loading the
current flow.

flow_id.description: The flow this run belongs to.

instance_id.description:
The agent instance this run belongs to, when a schedule armed one. Pod-local
and never published — see [`crate::flow_bindings`]. Absent on ad-hoc runs and
on records written before agent instances existed, which resume as before.

oneOf.description: Pause details when `status == "paused"`.

persona.description: Persona/model/cwd needed to resume the run.

variables.description: The run's state (`variables`) at the checkpoint.

warnings.description:
Non-fatal warnings computed when the run started — e.g. required packs/personas
that aren't installed or enabled. Surfaced in flow-debug UIs so a run that can't
fully work says why. Empty (and omitted) when the flow has everything it needs.

FlowRunSummary.description: The result of running (or pausing) a flow.

chat_id.description:
The conversation this run wrote itself into, so a caller can link a run
straight to its transcript. Absent for a run with no agent, and for a
tool-only flow that never spoke.

run_id.description: The run id (matches the `runs/{id}.json` record when the run paused).

warnings.description:
Missing-dependency warnings for this run (empty when the flow has everything
it needs). Shown in flow-debug UIs.

FlowStep.description: One node's contribution to the run trace.

detail.description: Optional human-readable detail (answer snippet, error, chosen handle).

flow.description: The raw template flow JSON, ready to be cloned and edited as a new flow.

FlowValidation.description: What is wrong with a flow graph, without saving it.

errors.description: One sentence per problem, in the validator's own words.

valid.description:
True when the graph would save. An editor enables its save button on this
rather than on an empty `errors`, so a future non-fatal warning does not
silently start blocking saves.

GatewayEvent.description:
One inbound or outbound gateway event.

`channel_id` is `None` when an inbound message matched no enabled channel —
these "unrouted" records are what make the global Network view useful for
diagnosing misconfiguration (e.g. a wrong `integration_id`).

channel_id.description: The matched gateway channel's id, or `None` if unrouted.

channel_name.description: The matched gateway channel's name, for display.

detail.description: Extra context — persona used, error message, etc.

source_id.description: Upstream gateway integration UUID (`source_id`), when known.

ts.description: RFC3339 timestamp; filled in by [`record`] if left empty.

GatewayStatus.description: What the workshop Connect panel renders from.

configured.description: The pod has a token (is linked to a Metalcraft ID account).

connected.description: A local `metalcraft-gateway` channel is enabled and the webhook secret is set.

has_public_url.description: Whether the pod knows its own public URL (POD_PUBLIC_URL) for the webhook.

registered.description: The user has registered a personal number on the gateway.

streaming.description:
The Inbound Pull long-poll is currently connected and draining. Unlike `connected`
(config present on disk), this is *intrinsic* liveness — it cannot be true while
inbound delivery is actually dead. `false` in push mode (no long-poll runs).

verified.description: That number is verified — required before connecting.

webhook_stale.description:
The gateway's registered inbound webhook (`consumer_webhook_url`) no longer
points at this pod's current URL, so inbound messages are being delivered into
the void. `connected` can be true while this is true — the "green light, dead
pipe" state. Detecting it kicks off a reactive re-register (see `status`).

HttpApiToolConfig.description: JSON config schema for a user-defined HTTP API tool.

oneOf.description:
Present only when `body_mapping == "multipart"`: describes which argument
carries the local file path and what form-field name to send it under.

param_paths.description:
Present only when `body_mapping == "params_nested"`: maps each flat
argument name to a dotted JSON path in the request body (e.g.
`"prompt": "payload.structured_data.params.prompt"`). Lets a tool expose
simple scalar parameters (which OpenAI's function-schema validation
accepts) while still producing a deeply nested JSON body — without the
string-substitution hazards of `body_mapping == "template"`. Arguments
with no entry here are inserted at the top level under their own name.
Absent (optional) arguments are simply skipped, and `body_defaults`
provides the nested base the paths are written onto.

poll.description:
Marks this tool as a status **poll** (e.g. checking an async job until it
finishes). Polling means calling the same tool with the same arguments
repeatedly on purpose, which would otherwise look like a runaway loop, so
the step guard exempts poll tools from tight loop detection. See
[`crate::guard`].

timeout_secs.description:
How long to wait on this tool's HTTP request, in seconds. Defaults to
[`DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECS`], which suits an API that answers in one round
trip and is far too short for one that holds the request open while it
works — a remote build, a clone, a container coming up. Those failed in
the *tool* while the server was still succeeding, which is the worst
shape of failure: the agent sees an error for work that then completes.
Clamped to [`MAX_TIMEOUT_SECS`]; `0` and anything unparseable fall back
to the default, so a typo cannot disable the bound.

InferenceStatus.description:
Whether this pod can run a turn, and on whose credential.

The one question a client cannot answer from `GET /api/v1/keys`: that endpoint
lists `keys.json`, and a provisioned pod's credential is injected as container
env, so a healthy pod reads as an empty store. Clients that inferred "no key,
cannot think" from it told people their working pod was dead. The pod is the
only honest source, so it answers here — through the same function a turn uses.

base_url.description:
Where inference is routed, userinfo and query stripped. Absent means the
default, OpenAI proper.

credential.description:
Which credential answered — `"stored"` (bound through this API),
`"environment"` (injected by provisioning, or a `.env`), `"pod_token"`
(this pod's own identity, offered only at the gateway), or `"none"`.

gateway.description: Routed at the Metalcraft gateway — so turns bill the account's credits.

ready.description:
A credential resolves, so a turn has something to authenticate with. This
is not a promise the turn *succeeds*: the gateway still meters credits and
requires the account's premium, which the pod cannot see.

flow.description: The flow whose dependencies were checked.

slug.description: Registry slug of the flow to install (equals the flow id).

InstallReport.description:
What an install actually did. Every field here is something a human or a UI has
a reason to see — silence about a skipped dependency is how you get an agent that
half works.

flows_installed_unscheduled.description:
Flows the pack shipped. **Every one lands disabled and unarmed** — installing
an identity must not start background work, and arming is the separate consent
moment that mints the agent to run it.

missing_env.description:
Credentials the pod does not have yet. A **warning**, never a failure: the
pack installs, its tools error clearly at call time, and `key_set` fixes it.

packs_deduplicated.description: Packs already present under the same hash — free, because content-addressed.

packs_stored.description: Packs newly written to the content store.

preset_collisions.description: Preset slugs already provided by another installed pack.

InstallResult.description: The result of a successful install: what landed + what it still needs.

agent_preset.description:
The agent preset this flow was bound to, chosen because its roster covers
every persona the flow names. `None` means no installed preset can reach them
all — the flow is saved and runnable by hand, but cannot be armed until one
can, which is worth saying at install rather than discovering later.

suggested_schedules.description:
Schedules the author suggests for this flow. **Nothing was scheduled** —
installing a flow starts no background work, which is now a property of the
format rather than a flag this path has to remember to clear. A client
offers these; a person accepting one creates the schedule.

InstalledFlow.description: Summary of the flow that was written.

scheduled.description:
What this agent is scheduled to do — the schedules armed to it. A pod
could not previously answer that question about a background agent.

InstanceListItem.description:
An agent in a list, with the one derived number a list actually needs.

Typed rather than patched into a `serde_json::Value` so it reaches the spec —
`conversation_count` was invisible to both generated clients, which is how a
field that exists on the wire can still be unusable.

InstanceMemoryView.description: What one agent knows, split by where it came from.

base.description: `<preset>@<version>` when this agent was shipped a knowledge base.

forgotten.description: Shipped memories this agent has been told to forget.

shipped.description: Memories the pack gave it, still visible (tombstones excluded).

oneOf.description:
A conversation with one person on one channel.

Keyed by sender, not just by channel: an agent's memory is the continuity
it exists to have, and one agent per *number* meant everything it learned
about everyone who texted in went into a single shared memory. `sender` is
the normalized key (see `gateway_sender_key`), not the raw `From` — the
same person must not get a second agent because their number arrived
formatted differently.

`None` on records written before this was per-sender; they keep working as
the channel's catch-all agent until they age out.

InstanceOrigin.description:
Where an instance came from.

Provenance only, since agents are never deleted on a timer — it answers "why
does this exist" (and, for `Gateway`, *who* it belongs to), not "how long does
it last".

IntegrationRef.description: A vendored integration, pinned by content.

content_sha256.description: Integrity pin for the vendored copy. Verified at install.

source.description: Where the author obtained it, for provenance display. Never fetched from.

personas.description: Number of personas/skills/api_tools/flow_templates the pack provides.

KeyEntry.description:
A stored key with its **scope** and whether it is managed (platform- or
connection-owned → read-only in the UI). Returned by `GET /api/v1/keys` so
the Keys page can group global keys and per-channel secrets, and lock the
managed ones. `channel_id`/`channel_name` are present only for channel scope.

KeyRevealResponse.description: The raw value of a key, returned only by the explicit reveal endpoint.

channel_id.description: When set, target this channel's secret scope instead of global.

KeySummary.description:
A stored API key, exposed to the workshop with its value masked — the
raw secret is never sent over the wire. Used by the load-time snapshot and
the sidebar (global scope only).

channel_id.description:
When set, the key is written to this channel's secret scope instead of
the global namespace.

agent_packs.description:
Agent packs — the unit of installation. Self-contained, so restoring these
needs no dependency ordering: each carries its own integrations.

version.description: Lockfile format version (not the artifacts' versions).

LockEntry.description: One pinned artifact in the lockfile.

content_sha256.description: Integrity hash of the installed content (verified on restore).

name.description: Registry slug (== pack id / flow id).

source.description: Registry origin the artifact came from (e.g. `https://packs.metalcraftai.com`).

MemoriesRef.description: Reference to the seed memories an agent pack ships with a preset.

origin.description: `"shipped"` or `"learned"` — the distinction the UI actually needs.

connection_token.description:
Audience-scoped connection token from the k3 broker, adopted as the
channel's outbound API key. Omitted on the Workshop path.

webhook_base.description: Override for the pod's public URL when `POD_PUBLIC_URL` isn't injected.

ModelFloor.description:
A **capability floor**, not a model name.

A hard `"gpt-5.4"` breaks on a pod that doesn't have it. Declare what the agent
needs and let the pod map that onto what it has; `prefer` is a hint, never a
requirement.

MultipartConfig.description:
Config for a `multipart/form-data` upload tool. The argument named by
`file_param` is treated as a local file path (constrained to the upload
root) and sent as the file part `file_field`; all other arguments become
text fields.

file_field.description: Multipart field name the server expects the file under (e.g. `"file"`).

file_param.description: Incoming argument that holds the local file path to upload.

persona_slug.description: Start this conversation as a specific persona from the agent's roster.

account.description: Whatever Octaweave will say about the account — an email or a name.

detail.description: The host's own words when something went wrong, shown rather than paraphrased.

link_url.description:
Where a human goes to finish it. Octaweave's own answer when it offers one,
falling back to its account page — the page that hosts the link button.

pack_installed.description:
Whether the tools are actually installed. Connecting without the pack reaches
nothing, and installing the pack without connecting authenticates as nobody —
a panel needs both facts to say which half is missing.

OctaweaveConnectionState.description:
How far this pod got with Octaweave, in the terms a panel can act on.

Named for its service rather than `ConnectionState`, because `utoipa` keys the
OpenAPI document by type name: a second `Connection` does not conflict loudly, it
**silently replaces** the first, and the generated client then types one endpoint
against another endpoint's shape.

Orphaned.description: One agent whose preset was withdrawn by an update.

frozen.description: Personas and skills copied into the user-local layer so the agent still runs.

PackInstallOutcome.description: Outcome of trying to satisfy one pack requirement of a flow.

detail.description: Human-readable detail (why it was skipped/failed, or the resolved version).

version.description: The version installed (or already present), when known.

content_sha256.description:
Optional integrity lock: the exact canonical content hash (64 lowercase
hex chars) the author resolved against. When set, a host may refuse to
install a pack whose content hash differs.

id.description:
Pack id / slug — the stable identity. Must match
`^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}$`.

optional.description:
When `true`, an unmet requirement is a warning rather than a hard failure —
the flow is expected to degrade gracefully.

reason.description: Human-readable reason, surfaced in an install/enable prompt.

resolved_version.description:
The concrete version the authoring environment resolved to, recorded as a
reproducibility hint (a lock). Advisory; hosts may re-resolve within
[`version`](Self::version).

version.description:
Semver range the pack must satisfy, e.g. `">=1.2.0, <2.0.0"`. `None` means
any installed version is acceptable.

persona.description: Move within the preset's roster. Rejected if the persona isn't in it.

PauseInfo.description: Why a run is paused and what will resume it.

message.description: For `approval`: the (interpolated) prompt shown to the human.

resume_handles.description:
For `approval`: the decision handles a human may choose. For `wait`:
typically `["after"]`.

wake_at.description: For `wait`: RFC-3339 timestamp at/after which the run may resume.

integrations.description:
Integrations this persona is scoped to, by id (e.g. `"linear"`). Every
HTTP-API tool an installed integration listed here provides is added to
the persona's tool set, so a persona can adopt a whole integration without
enumerating each `<id>_*` tool by name. Combine with `tools` for native
tools like `load_skill`. See [`Persona::resolved_tool_names`].

Reads `packs` too: that was the field's name until integrations stopped
being installable, and personas carrying it are already on people's pods.

max_run_secs.description:
How long a `sub_agent` delegation to this persona may run, in seconds.

The delegation guard has to bound a runaway sub-agent, but the right bound
is a property of the work: a persona that provisions a remote workspace
waits one to two minutes before it can do anything at all, while one that
edits a file should never take that long. A persona that knows it is slow
says so here instead of every pod having to be reconfigured for it.
Absent means the delegation default. See [`crate::tools::sub_agent`].

version.description:
Optional semantic version (e.g. "1.1.0") for built-in/seed personas.
Drives force-upgrade on startup: when a bundled seed persona's version
is higher than the installed copy's (a missing version counts as 0),
the installed file is overwritten. User-created personas omit this and
are never force-upgraded. See `seed::write_versioned_seeds`.

PersonaFallback.description: One agent whose persona was withdrawn by an update.

from.description: The persona the new version no longer provides.

to.description: The preset's new default, which it now uses instead.

PersonaRole.description: What a persona is allowed to do inside a preset.

pack_id.description:
Set when this persona is provided by an enabled integration.
Local (user-owned) personas omit this.

read_only.description: True for pack-provided personas — the workshop disables Save/Delete.

persona.description:
The persona this step is meant for. Advisory — the gate never checks that
the delegation actually went there, because a plan that reroutes mid-turn
is a plan working as intended.

step.description: What this step does, in one line, concrete enough to tell whether it happened.

PodSettings.description:
Everything a pod is configured to prefer.

Every field optional and every absence meaningful, because this file is
written by whichever client last saved and read by a pod that may be newer
than it: an unknown field must not become an opinion.

timezone.description:
IANA timezone this pod's people live in — `"America/Detroit"`.

Used for a cron schedule that names no zone of its own. `None` falls back
to the host clock, which is what every pod did before this existed and is
almost never what anybody meant.

PresetDetail.description:
A preset with its roster resolved against what this pod actually has.

Typed rather than assembled ad hoc so it reaches `openapi.json`: both Workshop
frontends generate their client types from the spec, and a response described only
by a prose `description` gives them nothing to generate.

library.description:
Not startable — see [`AgentPreset::library`]. Summaries still carry library
presets (installing over one is still a slug collision, and the UI has a
reason to show what a pack brought); a picker filters on this.

schedule.description: The trigger to project. Need not correspond to anything saved.

agent_instances.description:
Agents that actually exist. Ephemeral ones are excluded — an unfiltered list
is one row per chat ever started, which is noise, not information.

agent_presets.description:
Agents this pod can be. Both Workshop clients paint their agent picker from
the snapshot, so leaving these out costs an extra round-trip on every load.

flows.description:
From the external `metalcraft-flows` crate, which has no `ToSchema`; the
web app doesn't consume this field, so expose it as an opaque object array.

RecommendedKey.description:
A key recommended by one or more *enabled* integrations (from their
`requires_env`), with whether it currently resolves (key store or env) and
which packs declare it. Drives the "keys these packs still need" list in
the key store UI — `configured: false` is the hint to add it.

managed.description:
Platform-managed (env-authoritative, e.g. `METALCRAFT_TOKEN` injected into a
provisioned pod). The UI should show it as provided/read-only rather than
prompting the user to paste a value.

Registries.description:
Where this pod is willing to fetch an agent pack from.

Returned rather than only enforced so a UI can say what it accepts *before* the
user pastes a link and gets refused — and so a picker can offer the configured
hosts by name rather than making somebody remember an origin.

origins.description: Bare origins, kept for clients written against the earlier shape.

packs.description:
Integration packs this flow needs, each with an optional version/hash
contract.

tools.description:
Flat tool names the flow invokes (the real API surface — `tool` nodes bind
by bare name). Auto-derived by [`derive_requires`].

ResetFailure.description: A single entry the wipe could not remove.

name.description: Entry name, relative to the data dir.

ResetReport.description:
What the reset actually did — reported rather than assumed.

A partial wipe is a real outcome (a busy file, a read-only mount, a
permission the container lost), and it is the outcome where "success" is the
most dangerous thing to say: the operator would go on to test onboarding
against a pod that still has half its state.

data_dir.description: The data directory that was emptied.

failed.description:
Entries that could not be removed. Non-empty means the pod is *not*
factory-fresh, whatever the HTTP status said.

kept.description: Entry names deliberately left in place by the scope.

removed.description: Entry names removed, sorted. Directory entries count once.

restart.description: Whether the process expects to be restarted for it, or left down.

ResetScope.description: How much of the pod to take away.

RestartExpectation.description: What the pod expects to happen to it after the wipe.

RestoreResult.description: Wrapper for the lockfile-restore response (`{ outcomes: [...] }`).

data.description: Optional value to set as the resumed node's `_last` input.

handle.description: Handle to take (an approval decision, or `"after"` for a wait).

RosterPersona.description:
One entry in a preset's roster.

`installed: false` is the interesting case: the preset names a persona this pod
does not have. A UI should render it disabled with its `error` rather than
silently omit it — omission looks like the preset is smaller than it is.

error.description: Why it could not be resolved. Present only when `installed` is false.

RunFlowOutput.description:
The run endpoint returns one of two shapes depending on the flow's spec
version: v2 (state-machine) flows return a [`FlowRunSummary`]; v1 (linear)
flows return a [`RunFlowResponse`]. Documented as a `oneOf` so generated
clients see a proper union rather than an opaque object. Never constructed —
it exists only to describe the response schema.

inputs.description:
Values for the flow's declared entry `inputs`. Object of `{ name: value }`;
an input not named here falls back to its declared default, and a required
one with no default is left unset — a warning on the run rather than a
refusal to start it, so a flow can always be tried. Ignored by v1 flows.

instance_id.description:
Run as this agent, so the run recalls from and writes to its memory and
leaves a conversation behind. Omitted resolves from the flow's armed
schedules — see [`instance_for_manual_run`].

persona_slug.description:
Optional persona override. A v2 flow owns its persona via the entry node,
so this is normally omitted and left to the flow. It is only a fallback for
a flow that declares none (and for legacy v1 flows). Prompt nodes that
declare their own persona override it regardless.

SavedFlow.description:
A persisted flow document — what a `.json` file on disk contains.

A flow describes **what work is this**, and nothing else. When it runs, as
whom, and on which agent live in [`ScheduledFlow`](crate::scheduled::ScheduledFlow)
documents that point at it by id. A flow with no `ScheduledFlow` pointing at
it cannot fire — which is what makes "installing something never starts
background work" a property of the format rather than a rule every install
path has to remember.

oneOf.description:
Declared integration-pack / tool dependencies. Absent on legacy documents;
see [`crate::requires`].

spec_version.description: Spec version this document conforms to. Defaults to `"1"` when absent.

SchedulePreview.description: Projected firing times for a trigger — `description` plus the next few runs.

next_runs.description:
Next few firing times as RFC-3339 strings. Empty for a manual trigger, and
for a cron this pod cannot parse — which is the visible symptom of a
schedule that will never fire.

ScheduleSpecDoc.description:
Wire shape of [`metalcraft_flows::ScheduleSpec`], for the document only. See
[`ScheduledFlowDoc`] — same reason, same deal with drift.

The trigger is flattened onto the object and tagged by `type`, so a cron
schedule is `{ "type": "cron", "cron": "0 8 * * *" }` rather than carrying a
nested trigger object.

cron.description:
Present for `cron`. A standard cron expression; the pod parses it, the
spec crate does not.

inputs.description:
Inputs handed to the flow when this fires, so one flow can run with
different parameters on different schedules.

interval.description: Present for `minutes` and `hours`. Must be positive.

name.description:
Human-readable label ("Morning brief") — what a UI shows, and what the pod
names a minted agent after.

persona.description: Persona override for runs this schedule starts.

timezone.description:
IANA timezone the `cron` trigger is evaluated in. Ignored by other
triggers, and `null` means the pod's own time.

ScheduledFlowDoc.description:
What a [`metalcraft_flows::ScheduledFlow`] looks like on the wire, for the
OpenAPI document only.

**Nothing constructs one.** It exists because `ScheduledFlow` lives in the
`metalcraft-flows` crate and does not derive `ToSchema`, so the only way to
describe it here was `value_type = Object` — and an `Object` is not a gap in
the generated client, it is a hole that swallows its neighbours. utoipa emits
`Record<string, never>` for it, and TypeScript intersects that index signature
with the fields beside it: `id: string` becomes `string & never`. Every client
that generates from this document lost `id`, `flow_id`, `enabled` and
`schedule` — the whole stored half of every scheduled-flow response, including
the id needed to address one.

A mirror rather than a `ToSchema` derive on the real type because the real type
is in a published crate, and describing our own API should not require cutting
a release of somebody else's. The cost is that a mirror can drift from what it
mirrors, so it does not get to: `scheduled_flow_schema_matches_the_artifact`
serializes a real `ScheduledFlow` and fails if the two disagree about field
names. When `metalcraft-flows` next derives `ToSchema`, delete this and point
`value_type` at the real thing.

enabled.description:
Whether it fires. The only switch there is — the flow no longer knows it is
scheduled, so there is no flow-level master switch to disagree with.

flow_id.description:
The flow this runs, by its `id`. May dangle: the flow can be deleted out
from under it, which is why `flow_name` is optional on the row.

from_suggestion.description: The author suggestion this was created from. Provenance, not identity.

instance_id.description:
The agent it runs as, so successive firings accumulate memory instead of
waking up amnesiac.

schedule.description: The trigger and its per-schedule overrides.

allOf.description:
The artifact exactly as stored, so an editor can round-trip it without a
second representation of the same thing.

flow_name.description:
Name of the flow it runs. **Absent when that flow no longer exists** — a
schedule that can never fire, which is worth showing as broken rather than
quietly listing as fine.

instance_name.description:
Name of the agent it runs as. Absent if the instance was deleted out from
under it.

next_fire_at.description:
Next projected fire time, or absent for a manual trigger — and for a cron
this pod cannot parse, which is how a schedule that will never fire looks.

ScheduledFlowRow.description:
One scheduled flow, resolved for display: the stored document plus the three
things a client would otherwise have to compute or fetch.

SearchHit.description:
One result from a host's `/search`.

Everything past the name is optional because a fetch-only host is a real
deployment rather than a degenerate one (§11.1 makes `/search` optional in the
first place). A browse list renders what it got; it does not refuse what it
didn't.

id.description: The id on this host, without the `@`.

reference.description:
What to install: `axoniac:@amy_kitchen`. **Qualified, always** — an
unqualified reference is an error the moment two configured hosts publish the
same id (§11.3), and a browse list is precisely where that collision surfaces.

verified.description:
Whether the host vouches for it — worth exactly as much as the host's `trust`
makes it worth, and on a `verified-only` host it is what decides whether this
pod will install the pack at all.

SetEnabledRequest.description:
Kept only so the retired endpoint below still documents the body clients used
to send; the value is ignored.

SkillSummary.description: Summary of a skill for listings (no body).

pack_id.description: Set when this skill is provided by an enabled integration.

read_only.description: True for pack-provided skills — the workshop disables Save/Delete.

TimezoneRegion.description: One region's worth of timezones, for a picker that groups them.

zones.description: Full zone names in that area, sorted: `"America/Detroit"`.

Trust.description: How much a host's word is worth.

orphaned_agents.description:
Agents left pointing at a preset that no longer exists. Never silently
deleted — someone's memories are in there.

secret.description: New secret; omit or leave empty to keep the existing one.

UpdateReport.description: What an update did, beyond what the install did.

memory_bases_repointed.description: Agents whose shipped knowledge now points at the new version's base layer.

orphaned.description: Live agents whose preset was withdrawn (§12.3).

personas_fell_back.description: Live agents whose persona was withdrawn and fell back (§12.3).

enabled.description:
Pause (`false`) or resume (`true`) without deleting. The agent and its
memory are untouched either way.

instance_id.description: Move this schedule to a different agent.

oneOf.description: Replace the trigger and its overrides.
